final_candidates.decision_summary: Neutral isosteric replacement of the primary substrate-coordinating carboxylate in TM10 abolishes organic cation translocation while maintaining protein folding and membrane localization.
Alanine substitution removes the critical negative charge required for substrate binding, eliminating transport activity across substrates while preserving membrane expression.
Abolishes key cation-pi interactions in the central binding cavity (TM4), severely impairing transport activity without destabilizing transporter folding or assembly.

stop_reason.detail: Optimal Top-3 mutations identified and verified against sequence and biochemical consensus; no further iteration required.

history.rationale: Asp473 (canonical Asp474) in TM11 provides the essential negative charge for organic cation substrate binding. The isosteric D473N mutation neutralizes this charge and abolishes transport while preserving folding and plasma membrane localization.

D473 is the primary essential acidic residue in the TM10 binding pocket; its neutral isostere D473N reliably abolishes organic cation translocation while maintaining native-like folding and membrane trafficking.
Alanine substitution at TM11 Asp473 removes the primary carboxylate required for coordinating cationic substrates, abolishing transport activity while maintaining protein abundance.
Alanine scanning at D473 strips the required negative charge for substrate coordination, completely eliminating transport function while preserving stability in the membrane.

Trp216 in TM4 mediates essential cation-pi interactions in the central binding cleft. Mutation to alanine severely impairs substrate translocation while preserving transmembrane alpha-helical packing.

W216 in TM4 is a core aromatic residue essential for cation-pi interaction in substrate translocation, and its substitution to alanine severely impairs transport while preserving overall architecture.

Arg171 belongs to the conserved cytoplasmic motif A charge-pair network between TM2 and TM3. Alanine substitution disables the alternating-access rocker-switch mechanism, arresting transport without destabilizing the fold.
Part of the intracellular gate charge-relay network (D170-R171 motif); disruption abolishes rocker-switch alternating access without destabilizing the fold.

Arg398 is the invariant basic residue of the TM8-TM9 motif A network that coordinates cytoplasmic gating during transport. Mutating it to alanine abolishes transport cycles while preserving expression.
Conserved intracellular loop 4/TM8-9 salt bridge residue; mutation freezes or impairs conformational transitions required for substrate transport.

Asp170 forms critical inter-helical salt bridges in motif A that govern conformational transitions. Alanine mutation disrupts cytoplasmic gating and abolishes transport while maintaining protein stability.
Directly partners with R171 in cytoplasmic gating, crucial for transport mechanism while leaving general transmembrane packing intact.
Asp397 is the acidic partner in the TM8-TM9 intracellular gate network. Neutralizing this residue impedes the conformational transitions required for substrate transport while preserving abundance.
Forms the symmetrical cytoplasmic salt-bridge triad complementary to D170-R171, critical for catalytic transport cycle.
Arg174 is an integral component of the motif A salt-bridge triad stabilizing inward- and outward-facing intermediates. Its mutation blocks substrate translocation without inducing misfolding.
Adjacent positively charged residue involved in cytoplasmic gating and membrane topology maintenance.
Arg401 contributes to the symmetrical cytoplasmic charge network stabilizing MFS conformational transitions. Substitution with alanine inactivates transport cycling with minimal impact on expression.
Contributes to the cytoplasmic basic cluster; loss reduces transport rate but has higher risk of incomplete inactivation than D473 mutations.
Glu454 lines the TM10 permeation pathway and facilitates substrate passage. Mutating it to alanine disrupts polar translocation interactions while retaining normal membrane insertion.
Conserved polar/charged residue in TM9; alanine mutation decreases transport rate, though less completely than primary binding pocket mutants.
